introduction: ERC-926 defines one registry that maps any address to a metadata provider contract, so any account or contract can publish its own metadata. It was proposed by Nick Johnson in March 2018. Rather than store values directly, it uses indirection: setProvider records the caller's provider and provider returns it, and each provider exposes typed record interfaces via ERC-165. Note: ERC-926 is Stagnant — it has been inactive for 6+ months and may never be finalized, but remains historically or technically significant.
designPurpose: ERC-926 was designed to stop the proliferation of single-purpose registry contracts. Before it, use cases such as generalised authorisations, token acceptance settings, and claims registries each deployed their own storage contract, so callers had to know a different address and layout for every kind of metadata. By standardizing one registry that returns a per-address provider, ERC-926 lets new metadata types be added as separate provider interfaces without redeploying a shared key/value schema.
commonUsage: The registry targets applications that attach structured data to an address, such as generalised authorization schemes, token acceptance preferences, and claims or reputation records. Because a provider can implement any subset of standardized record-type interfaces and advertise them through ERC-165, wallets, dapps, and indexers query one fixed registry address, follow the indirection to the provider, and read only the record types they understand. As a Stagnant proposal it saw little production use.
fn.provider.desc: Returns the address of the metadata provider contract currently registered for the supplied address, or the zero address if none has been set.
fn.provider.params.target: The address whose registered metadata provider is being queried.
fn.provider.returns.provider: The provider contract registered for the queried address, or the zero address when unset.
fn.setProvider.desc: Registers the metadata provider contract for the caller's own address, overwriting any previous provider. The registry keys the entry by msg.sender, so an address can only set its own provider.
fn.setProvider.params.provider: The metadata provider contract to associate with the caller's address.
sim.registerProviderWalkthrough.name: Register & Resolve Provider
sim.registerProviderWalkthrough.desc: Follow an address registering its metadata provider and a consumer resolving it through the registry.
sim.registerProviderWalkthrough.step.set: The address owner calls setProvider(_provider) on the registry to register its chosen metadata provider contract.
sim.registerProviderWalkthrough.step.sto: The registry writes the provider into the provider mapping under the caller's address, replacing any earlier entry.
sim.registerProviderWalkthrough.step.loo: A consumer calls provider(target) and the registry reads the mapping, returning the registered provider address.
